name: 吉野本葛 天極堂 奈良本店 (Yoshino Honkuzu Tengyokudo Nara Honten)

claims.text: Not a dedicated gluten-free kitchen; the house specialty 葛うどん (kuzu udon) is made with wheat noodles, so wheat is handled on site.
Pure kuzu (Yoshino arrowroot starch) is naturally gluten-free, and several signature items — kuzu mochi, kuzu kiri and kuzu yu — are starch-based sweets rather than wheat-based.

name: 吉野葛 佐久良 (Yoshino Kuzu Sakura)

claims.text: Signature dishes are made from 100% Yoshino hon-kuzu (arrowroot), a naturally gluten-free and plant-based starch, prepared fresh to order.
Menu is dominated by breaded, deep-fried cutlets, hamburg steak and omurice; no separate fryer or gluten-free preparation is documented, so heavy wheat cross-contact should be assumed.
Kitchen is centered on meat and fish; shared surfaces and likely meat/fish-based stocks make this unsuitable for strict vegans, and no plant-based dishes are documented.

name: 海女小屋 ちさと (Amagoya Chisato)

claims.text: Soy sauce is commonly offered as a finishing condiment at hama-yaki shellfish grills; standard soy sauce contains wheat. No gluten-free soy sauce is documented here, so a celiac should request shellfish grilled plain without soy sauce.
The core offering is shellfish and lobster grilled plainly over charcoal, which at the ingredient level is naturally free of gluten and easy to order without added sauces.

name: あみ焼き 天びん屋 (Amiyaki Tenbinya)

claims.text: Grill-your-own format with shared grills and tongs creates cross-contact between seafood, sauced meats, and naturally GF items; no separate surface documented.
Menu includes shrimp tempura and other fried items; no dedicated fryer mentioned.
Grilled meats served with soy-based tare or miso sauce, which typically contain wheat.
Grilled vegetables cooked on grills shared with oysters, shellfish, and meat.
Naturally simpler items can be eaten plain: oyster gangan-yaki, grilled shellfish, grilled vegetables.

name: ブランカ 鳥羽本店 (Blanca Toba Honten)

claims.text: 看板商品シェルレーヌの原材料に小麦粉が含まれ、焼き菓子全般が小麦ベース。グルテンフリー製品や専用調理の記載はなく、共有設備での製造とみられます。
主力商品はバター（乳）と卵を使用する焼き菓子で、植物性のみの商品は確認できませんでした。
シェルレーヌの特定原材料（小麦・乳・卵・アーモンド）が明記されており、含有アレルゲンを事前に確認できます。
Crepes are cooked on a shared griddle/hot plate; the batter is wheat flour, so the product is inherently not gluten-free and cross-contamination with wheat is unavoidable.
Fillings/toppings can be customized to the customer's preference, which gives some flexibility in choosing what goes on the crepe (though not the wheat batter itself).

The venue is a confectionery production lab actively making wheat-based Belgian waffles and baked goods, so shared surfaces and high gluten cross-contamination risk should be assumed. No gluten-free protocol is published.
A soy latte is offered, giving vegans a plant-milk drink option alongside fruit juices and tea.
Puddings and confections are advertised as additive-free (無添加) using local Mie produce.
